title: Week Ahead — Market Outlook
headline: Markets enter a catalyst-heavy week with a two-sided setup: softer jobs data have cooled rate-hike bets, but Fed minutes, fresh activity and sentiment readings, Treasury supply and Middle East oil risk could quickly reverse the relief.
volatilityRationale: Moderate (6/10): the VIX closed at 15.31 on October 2, while recent Treasury-yield strain and Iran-related oil risk leave rates-sensitive assets exposed to shocks. Services data, FOMC minutes, Treasury auctions and consumer sentiment are stacked into five sessions, making this catalyst-heavy without evidence of panic pricing.

recap.text: For the week through October 2, the S&P 500 fell 0.3% and the Dow lost 1.3%, while the Nasdaq rose 0.5%; all three rallied on Friday after the September jobs report.
The September employment report showed payrolls up just 29,000 and unemployment at 4.2%, with employment little changed across major industries.

A September 28 risk-off session linked higher oil prices and Treasury yields to the U.S.-Iran standoff and Strait of Hormuz concerns; the 30-year Treasury yield touched its highest level since May 2004.

triggers.text: September ISM Services PMI release at 10:00 a.m. ET; the activity, prices and employment details may help distinguish a soft-patch signal from broader demand resilience.
Treasury auctions include a 3-year note on Tuesday, a 10-year reopening on Wednesday and a 30-year reopening on Thursday; investor demand could set the tone for duration and yields.
Federal Reserve minutes from the September 15–16 FOMC meeting are due at 2:00 p.m. ET, offering detail on the policy debate behind the decision.
The University of Michigan's preliminary October consumer sentiment results are scheduled for 10:00 a.m. ET; watch for updates on household outlook and price concerns.
U.S.-Iran and Strait of Hormuz headlines remain an unscheduled oil-market risk; any renewed shipping disruption could revive energy-inflation and rate concerns.

watch.text: Watch whether the VIX holds near its October 2 close of 15.31 or reprices as data and policy headlines land.
Compare the minutes and services reading with the labor-market softness that led traders to pare October rate-hike bets; a change in that rate narrative could quickly shift equity leadership.
Track oil and long-duration Treasury yields together: renewed Iran-related energy pressure could restore the inflation and financing-cost headwinds that weighed on stocks earlier in the week.
